diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-1 Brake system
diagrams.description: Chassis layout schematic showing hydraulic brake lines, master cylinder, Master-Vac, NP-valve, 3-way connector, front disc brakes, rear drum brakes, and hand brake control lever.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: NP-valve is connected between master cylinder rear outlet and rear wheel circuits to modulate hydraulic pressure and prevent rear lockup.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-2 Brake pedal mounting
diagrams.description: Brake pedal assembly mounted to pedal bracket under dashboard with stop lamp switch, fulcrum pin, and return spring.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fulcrum pin tightening torque: 3.5 to 4.0 kg-m (25 to 29 ft-lb).

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-3 Brake pedal components
diagrams.description: Exploded view of brake pedal arm, bushings, sleeve, fulcrum bolt, clevis pin, return spring, and pedal pad.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lubricate pedal shaft sleeve unit and clevis pin unit with multi-purpose grease.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-4 Adjusting brake pedal
diagrams.description: Diagram illustrating brake pedal height measurement from floor to pedal pad upper surface, lock nut, and stopper adjustment.
measurements_and_specs: 206 mm (8.11 in) with pedal stopper non-effected
203 mm (7.99 in) pedal height after stopper adjustment
15 mm (0.59 in) pedal depression for stop lamp switch illumination
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn back stopper to reduce pedal height from 206 mm (8.11 in) to 203 mm (7.99 in).

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-5 Master cylinder
diagrams.description: Exploded view of tandem master cylinder body, front/rear reservoirs, primary and secondary piston assemblies, check valves, and bleeder.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: NABCO and TOKIKO makes are not interchangeable. Match parts to the brand of the body.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-6 Cross-sectional view of master cylinder
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional cutaway diagram of tandem master cylinder showing internal passages, primary piston, secondary piston, return springs, check valve, and reservoir fluid ports.
measurements_and_specs: Allowable cylinder to piston clearance: max 0.15 mm (0.0059 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply clean brake fluid to cylinder bore and pistons, and light rubber grease to piston cups during reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-7 Brake line
diagrams.description: Schematic routing of galvanized steel brake tubes, flexible pressure hoses, 3-way connectors, NP-valve, and bridge tubes across chassis.
measurements_and_specs: Brake tube tightening torque: 1.5 to 1.8 kg-m (11 to 13 ft-lb)
Pressure hose tightening torque: 1.7 to 2.0 kg-m (12 to 14 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use flare nut torque wrench GG94310000. Ensure hoses do not contact tires or suspension members during steering and travel.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-8 Cross-sectional view of NP-valve
diagrams.description: Cutaway diagram of NP-valve (proportioning valve) showing internal plunger, lip seal, cup seal, spring, Y-seal, and inlet/outlet fluid paths.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Port connections: Master cylinder front side, Master cylinder rear side, To front wheel cylinder, To rear wheel cylinder.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-9 NP-valve
diagrams.description: External view of NP-valve showing body mounting and direction arrow mark for correct line installation.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Connect brake lines with 'F' mark toward front brake side and with arrow mark toward rear brake side.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-10 Front disc brake
diagrams.description: Exploded view of Girling-Sumitomo model S-16 front disc brake caliper assembly, pistons, seals, dust covers, pads, shims, and retaining hardware.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Anti-squeal shims are directional; install with arrow mark pointing in rotor forward rotating direction.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-11 Piston seal automatic adjusting operation
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional diagrams illustrating elastic deformation of piston seal during compression and return retraction during decompression.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Movement exceeding elastic displacement slips along seal surface for auto-adjustment; seal returns piston upon decompression.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-12 Removing pad
diagrams.description: Removal procedure of retaining clip, pin, anti-squeal spring, and brake pad from caliper.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove clip, slide out retaining pin, take off anti-squeal spring, then extract pads with shims.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-13 Applying grease
diagrams.description: Illustration indicating shaded areas on caliper guides and both sides of anti-squeal shims where brake grease must be applied, showing rotation arrow on shim.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply pad grease to working portions of caliper and both sides of shim. Ensure shim arrow points in forward rotor rotation direction. Never grease pad friction faces.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-14 Removing calipers
diagrams.description: Removing brake hydraulic line and two caliper mounting bolts from knuckle spindle.
measurements_and_specs: Caliper installation bolt torque: 7.3 to 9.9 kg-m (53 to 72 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use flare nut wrench on brake line.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-15 Removing piston
diagrams.description: Applying compressed air to caliper fluid inlet while retaining ring is removed to expel pistons.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Gradually apply compressed air. Hold smoother piston with wood block to extract both pistons evenly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-16 Measuring runout
diagrams.description: Dial indicator setup positioned at rotor pad contact surface centerline to measure total indicator runout while turning rotor.
measurements_and_specs: Runout limit: 0.10 mm (0.0039 in) Total indicator reading
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Wheel bearings must be correctly adjusted prior to runout measurement.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-17 Measuring parallelism
diagrams.description: Micrometer measurement taken around the circumference of brake rotor pad contact surface to determine parallelism / thickness variation.
measurements_and_specs: Parallelism limit: Less than 0.03 mm (0.0012 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure thickness at multiple points around entire periphery on the same circumference.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-18 Rear brake
diagrams.description: Exploded view of leading-trailing rear drum brake showing backing plate, wheel cylinder, brake shoes, return springs, anti-rattle pins, toggle lever, and automatic adjuster.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Front shoe lining is low; rear shoe lining is high. Fore-shoe is in trailing side and after-shoe is in leading side.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-19 Sectional view of rear brake
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional assembly drawing of rear drum brake mechanism showing wheel cylinder, shoe web engagement, adjuster strut, and drum contact.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Shows alignment of automatic adjuster strut between leading and trailing shoes.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-20 Adjuster assembly (Left-hand side)
diagrams.description: Exploded detail of left-hand brake automatic adjuster assembly, including threaded adjusting screw, sleeve, toggle lever, ratchet claw, and pivot pin.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjuster mechanisms differ between LH and RH sides; threads are side-specific.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-21 Removing toggle lever stopper
diagrams.description: Technique for removing cotter pin and stopper from toggle lever through the backing plate aperture when brake drum is stuck.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fully pull up center hand brake lever, push/tap out cotter pin to release stopper, then release lever to slacken shoes for drum removal.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-22 Applying brake grease
diagrams.description: Lube points on brake shoes, adjuster assembly, adjusting nut threads, and toggle lever contacts indicated by bold arrows.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply brake grease to adjuster sliding slots, threaded screw shaft, and shoe web contact tips. Do not contaminate friction linings.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-23 Applying brake grease
diagrams.description: Six lubrication points on the rear brake backing plate (brake disc) ledges and anchor block where brake shoe edges slide.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply thin layer of brake grease to the 6 shoe ledge contact pads on backing plate and anchor block.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-24 Removing wheel cylinder
diagrams.description: Disconnection of rear hydraulic brake line and removal of two wheel cylinder mounting bolts on backing plate.
measurements_and_specs: Wheel cylinder bolt torque: 0.6 to 0.8 kg-m (4.3 to 5.8 ft-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use flare nut wrench on brake line fitting.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-25 Wheel cylinder and adjustor
diagrams.description: Exploded view of rear wheel cylinder body, bleeder screw, dust boot, piston, cup seal, spring, and automatic adjuster strut with toggle lever.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: NABCO and TOKIKO wheel cylinders are not interchangeable. Match parts by manufacturer.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-26 Applying rubber grease to piston cup
diagrams.description: Cross section of wheel cylinder piston cup assembly showing application points for rubber grease along lip groove and sealing contact.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply rubber grease to cup grooves and lips prior to inserting into cylinder.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-27 Hand brake linkage
diagrams.description: Component layout of parking brake linkage showing control lever, front rod, center lever, equalizer, rear cables, wire hangers, and adjusting rod.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Linkage is located inside tunnel; propeller shaft removal required for access.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-30 Removing control lever
diagrams.description: Removal of center console boot fasteners and control lever pivot mounting bolt from passenger compartment floor.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove right-hand seat to remove control lever into cabin.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-28 Removal of hand brake
diagrams.description: Under-chassis view showing disconnection of adjusting rod nut, clevis pins, hanger spring, and four mounting bolts of center arm.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Center arm nuts are welded to floor panel.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-29 Removing rear cable
diagrams.description: Disconnection of parking brake cable from wheel brake backing plate toggle lever and removal of cable housing retainer clips.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove wheel-side retainers and equalizer-side retainer to withdraw cable.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-31 Cross-sectional view of Master-Vac
diagrams.description: Comparative cross-sectional cutaways of both M75 type (top) and M90 type (bottom) vacuum brake boosters detailing internal valves, reaction disc, power piston, and return springs.
components: Power piston (Valve body and diaphragm plate)

callouts.5: Power piston (Valve body and diaphragm plate)

diagrams.mechanic_notes: M75 type fitted to 2-seater models; M90 type fitted to 2+2 GS30 models.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-32 Installing vacuum gauge
diagrams.description: Connecting vacuum test gauge into line between check valve and Master-Vac booster.
measurements_and_specs: Test vacuum: 500 mmHg (19.69 inHg)
Max allowable drop in 15 sec: 25 mmHg (0.98 inHg)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Engine stopped at 500 mmHg; monitor drop after 15 seconds without braking and with full braking force.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-33 Removing check valve
diagrams.description: Location and removal of brake booster vacuum line check valve from engine compartment.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect spring clips at both ends to remove check valve.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-34 Cross-sectional view of check valve
diagrams.description: Cutaway view of check valve showing internal valve disc, spring, and flow direction from Master-Vac side to manifold side.
measurements_and_specs: Max allowable leak at 500 mmHg in 15 sec: 10 mmHg (0.39 inHg)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: One-way flow only: opens towards intake manifold side.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-35 Performance curve of Master-Vac (M90 type)
diagrams.description: Output performance graph for M90 (9-inch) booster plotting brake fluid pressure (psi, kg/cm²) against pedal operating force (kg, lb) at 500 mmHg and 0 mmHg vacuum.
measurements_and_specs: Test vacuum: 500 mmHg (19.69 inHg)
0 mmHg (0 inHg)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Knee point occurs at approximately 25-30 kg pedal force with 500 mmHg vacuum.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-36 Performance curve of Master-Vac (M75 type)
diagrams.description: Output performance graph for M75 (7.5-inch) booster plotting brake fluid pressure against pedal force at 500 mmHg and 0 mmHg vacuum.
measurements_and_specs: Test vacuum: 500 mmHg (19.69 inHg)
0 mmHg (0 inHg)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Knee point occurs at approximately 30-35 kg pedal force with 500 mmHg vacuum.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-37 Removal method of Master-Vac
diagrams.description: Numbered sequence for disconnecting pedal return spring, clevis pin, master cylinder nuts, and Master-Vac firewall mounting nuts.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove in numerical order 1 to 6.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-38 Removing rear shell
diagrams.description: Removal of operating rod clevis, lock nut, and rubber valve body guard.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove clevis, lock nut, and guard prior to unscrewing rear shell.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-39 Removing rear shell
diagrams.description: Using special tool Master-Vac Wrench ST08080000 to rotate and unlock rear shell from front shell lugs.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn tool counterclockwise to disengage interlocking shell tabs.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-40 Removing seal
diagrams.description: Prying off oil seal assembly from rear shell housing using a flat screwdriver.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not disassemble seal unless necessary; avoid scratching rear shell seat.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-41 Separating diaphragm
diagrams.description: Peeling rubber diaphragm bead out of the annular groove in bakelite diaphragm plate.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Detach diaphragm bead carefully to avoid tearing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-42 Removing air silencer retainer
diagrams.description: Prying air silencer retainer evenly out of diaphragm plate using screwdriver blade.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Never tap screwdriver with a hammer; pry evenly around retainer.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-43 Pulling out stop key
diagrams.description: Extracting valve plunger stop key from valve body hub while vibrating push rod.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Point key hole downward, lightly push rod and vibrate to disengage stop key.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-44 Removing valve operating rod assembly
diagrams.description: Withdrawing valve operating rod, silencer elements, and air valve plunger assembly from power piston.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Rod and plunger assembly are staked together and cannot be disassembled.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-45 Removing reaction disc
diagrams.description: Removing rubber reaction disc from center cavity of diaphragm plate.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Always replace reaction disc with a new one at each reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-46 Removing spacer
diagrams.description: Detaching mounting stud spacer from front shell housing using screwdriver.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pry spacer off front shell studs.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-47 Installing oil seal
diagrams.description: Pressing oil seal into rear shell using drift tool ST08090000 (9") or ST08060000 (7.5").
measurements_and_specs: Length 'A': 10.2 to 10.8 mm (0.402 to 0.425 in) for 9 in dia
Length 'A': 6.7 to 7.0 mm (0.264 to 0.276 in) for 7.5 in dia
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Align tool pawl with seal hole; drive until specified protrusion 'A' is achieved.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-48 Length at "A"
diagrams.description: Cross section showing seal depth dimension 'A' measured from retainer edge in rear shell.
measurements_and_specs: Length 'A': 10.2 to 10.8 mm (0.402 to 0.425 in) for 228.60 mm (9 in) diaphragm
Length 'A': 6.7 to 7.0 mm (0.264 to 0.276 in) for 190.50 mm (7.5 in) diaphragm
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Critical seal press depth dimension A.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-49 Requiring grease place
diagrams.description: Arrows pointing to outer cylindrical sliding surfaces of plunger assembly requiring Master-Vac grease.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply thin coat of Master-Vac grease to sliding periphery of plunger assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-50 Inserting stop key
diagrams.description: Pushing valve plunger stop key home into slot of bakelite diaphragm plate.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Diaphragm plate is bakelite; insert key gently without cracking plate.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-51 Tightening rear shell
diagrams.description: Turning rear shell clockwise using wrench ST08080000 until locking notches engage front shell tabs.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Align scribe marks, turn clockwise until tool reaches notch in shell retainer.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-52 Length at "B"
diagrams.description: Diagram illustrating push rod tip protrusion dimension 'B' beyond booster front shell mounting face.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust push rod tip length to 9.75 to 10.00 mm before mounting master cylinder.

diagrams.caption: Fig. BR-53 Adjusting push rod length
diagrams.description: Holding push rod serrations with pliers while turning adjusting screw tip with wrench.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lock push rod body securely to prevent turning inner diaphragm while adjusting tip.

diagrams.caption: GG94310000 Flare nut torque wrench
diagrams.description: Special flare nut torque wrench designed for hydraulic brake line fittings.
measurements_and_specs: Applicable to brake tube connectors
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Prevents rounding of flare nuts on tubing joints.

diagrams.caption: ST08080000 Master-Vac wrench
diagrams.description: Spanner wrench with locating pins to engage Master-Vac rear shell for opening and closing booster halves.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Used to twist and lock rear shell to front shell notches.

diagrams.caption: ST08060000 Master-Vac oil seal retainer drift (4.5", 6", 7.5")
diagrams.description: Flanged driver drift with alignment pawl for installing oil seal to precise depth 'A' in 7.5-inch Master-Vac rear shell.
measurements_and_specs: Depth A: 6.7 to 7.0 mm (0.264 to 0.276 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Applicable to 7 1/2" Master-Vac on 2-seater models.

diagrams.caption: ST08090000 Master-Vac oil seal retainer drift (9")
diagrams.description: Flanged driver drift with alignment pawl for installing oil seal to precise depth 'A' in 9-inch Master-Vac rear shell.
measurements_and_specs: Dia: 9"
Depth A: 10.2 to 10.8 mm (0.402 to 0.425 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Applicable to 9" Master-Vac on 2+2 seater models.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Swollen master cylinder seals due to poor fluid quality or contamination by kerosene, gasoline or mineral oil.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Flush the system, replace all rubber parts, refill with new fluid and air bleed the lines.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Pistons or valve carrier locked by deposits of fluid, foreign matter, etc.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clean and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Seized master cylinder piston due to infiltrations of water through rear end due to faulty boot or seals.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Service the master cylinder, replace the piston and the boot and/or seals, to prevent water infiltration.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Seized pedal shaft.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Smooth bushings, or if other sliding parts are damaged to a remarkable extent, replace them and lubricate.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Clogged transfer port.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Disassemble and clean master cylinder.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: No compensation takes place. Weak return spring.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace faulty spring.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Air in brake system because of imperfect bleeding.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Bleed thoroughly.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Swollen hose due to deterioration.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace the hose and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Hose swells under fluid pressure due to poor hose quality.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Fit new hoses and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Use of a poor quality brake fluid (boiling point of which is too low).
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace the fluid with the specified brake fluid and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Clogged reservoir filler cap vent hole. This promotes a vacuum in master cylinder that sucks air through rear seal.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clean reservoir filler cap and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Deteriorated check valve.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Fit a new check valve, make sure that there are no burrs, roughness or blow holes in master cylinder, and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Fluid leaks through connection.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Tighten connections, and if necessary, replace faulty parts. Bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Fluid leaks at wheel cylinders.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace the seals and packings being damaged. Wipe and clean brake shoe linings.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Fluid leaks through hoses.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace the damaged hose, and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Low fluid level in reservoir.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Add specified fluid up to correct level.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Master cylinder relief port clogged with foreign matter.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clean and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: System has not been bled.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Excessive clearance between shoes and drum.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Adjust auto-adjuster operation.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Fluid level in reservoir is too low.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Top up with specified brake fluid, bleed the system, if required.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Deteriorated rubber seals in master cylinder or in wheel cylinders.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace seals and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Excessively swollen hoses due to poor hose quality.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace by designated hoses and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Thermal expansion of drums due to excessive overheating.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Allow drums to cool off. Check brake shoe linings and drums. Replace damaged parts.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Worn or broken return spring.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace faulty springs.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Improper brake shoe return.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Grease brake shoe and wheel cylinder sliding surface.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Clogged master cylinder relief port.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clean and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Swollen or stuck rubber seals due to contamination by kerosene, mineral oil, gasoline, etc.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Flush the system, replace all rubber parts, refill with new brake fluid and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Fluid leakage at one wheel cylinder only.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Wipe, clean or replace the brake shoe linings or lining pads, service the wheel cylinder and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Rusted or corroded edges of a wheel cylinder.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Eliminate rust and replace the boots.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Seized piston in wheel cylinder or caliper assembly.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Service the wheel cylinder, replace the rear wheel cylinder piston or caliper assembly and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Hose obstructed due to swollen or clogged inner lining.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace or clean the hose and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Obstructed flow in metal pipe due to crushing or clogging (if the brakes on one axle are excluded, weak braking may result).
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace or clean the pipe and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty seals at one half caliper.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Take down and strip the half caliper, replace seals and dust covers.

troubleshooting.symptom: Brake linings dragging all the time on drums or brake discs
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Insufficient shoe-to-drum clearance.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Adjust clearance.

troubleshooting.symptom: Brake linings dragging all the time on drums or brake discs
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Weak shoe return springs.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace the springs.

troubleshooting.symptom: Brake linings dragging all the time on drums or brake discs
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Brake pedal has no free travel.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Set the push rod length as prescribed.

troubleshooting.symptom: Brake linings dragging all the time on drums or brake discs
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Seized master cylinder piston.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Service the master cylinder, replace the piston and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.symptom: Brake linings dragging all the time on drums or brake discs
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Master cylinder flooded due to clogged relief port.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Service the master cylinder, replace the check valve if deteriorated, clean the relief port and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.symptom: Brake linings dragging all the time on drums or brake discs
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Brake disc run-out.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check brake disc for run-out, and replace faulty parts, if necessary.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Fluid leakage from wheel cylinders.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Wipe and clean the brake shoe linings, service the wheel cylinder replacing damaged parts, and bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Fluid leakage from caliper cylinders.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Take down and strip the calipers; replace all rubber seals and clean lining pads.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Improper Master-Vac function due to poor vacuum.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check the pipe or hose connections, and fasten if necessary. Or replace a faulty vacuum hose.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Required vacuum is not maintained.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Wipe, clean or replace the check valve and check the grommet for loose fit, re-fit or replace it. Replace seal or retighten plate and seal assembly-to-front shell bolts. Clean or replace poppet rubber. Replace diaphragm and diaphragm plate.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Weak pressure on shoes due to use of too thick fluid.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Flush the system and refill with specified fluid. Bleed the system.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Dust on drums or linings soiled with oil.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Remove and clean drums thoroughly.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Weak shoe return springs.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check springs and replace as required.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Drum out of round.
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Correct drums by means of a lathe.
